notes: Oklahoma's All-State ensembles are split between two organizations. OkMEA's Choral Division administers the High School Mixed Chorus, High School Treble Chorus and the Intercollegiate Choir; its Elementary Division administers the Children's All-State Chorus. OkCDA (Oklahoma Choral Directors Association) separately administers Junior High Mixed Chorus, Junior High Treble Chorus, High School Show Choir and Vocal Jazz Ensemble. This record covers the OkMEA high school choruses, whose page was last updated July 17, 2026 and carries full 2026-27 information. Both All-State chorus rounds are published as 'Saturday, October 31' and 'Saturday, November 14' without a year; those weekdays match 2026 and sit between the September 2026 deadlines and the January 2027 festival. There is one audition process for both choruses: every interested student auditions for the Mixed Chorus and the committee places singers after the final round.

organization.name: Oklahoma Music Educators Association
organization.description: OkMEA is Oklahoma's state music education association. Its Choral Division administers the All-State High School Mixed Chorus, High School Treble Chorus and Intercollegiate Choir, and its Elementary Division administers the Children's All-State Chorus. All-State ensembles rehearse and perform at the annual January conference/festival.

programs.name: All-State Mixed Chorus and Treble Chorus
programs.description: OkMEA runs a single two-round audition process for both the All-State Mixed Chorus and the All-State Treble Chorus: every interested student auditions for the Mixed Chorus, and the committee places singers into the two ensembles after the final round. 2026-27 conductors are Dr. Frances Fonza (Southeastern Louisiana University) for the Mixed Chorus and Dr. Alissa Mercurio Rowe (Louisiana State University) for the Treble Chorus.

requirements.title: Current NAfME/OkMEA membership required
requirements.description: Directors must verify their NAfME/OkMEA membership is current; students cannot be entered for auditions without membership in the organization.

requirements.title: Non-traditional voice part registration
requirements.description: Students may audition on a non-traditional voice part (for example, a boy auditioning as an alto) only if the student consistently sings that part in their school's choral organization. The director must complete a Non-Traditional Voice Part Registration Form for each such student, notify the Mixed Chorus Chair by email, and scan/email the form to the chair or deliver it to the Quad Chair at the first round audition site. Completed forms must be received before the student attempts the first round audition.

requirements.title: Official rehearsal tracks
requirements.description: Student auditions use the official Rehearsal Tracks, which are purchased through OkCDA. The tracks, produced by Kevin Zinn, include pronunciation guides for foreign-language pieces, and are ordered via an online Rehearsal Track Order Form.

requirements.title: Two-round quadrant audition process
requirements.description: First round auditions are held at four quadrant sites (Northwest, Northeast, Southwest, Southeast); students who advance audition in a second round at a single statewide site. OkMEA instructs directors to arrive early, remain available to assist with the audition process as directed by the site manager, and observe scheduled audition times — a student who does not appear at the scheduled time is disqualified.

requirements.title: Fees escalate by deadline; deadlines strictly enforced
requirements.description: OkMEA states that most groups have three levels of fees — first deadline, second deadline and emergency — and that deadlines are strictly enforced, with a much higher per-student rate after the first deadline passes.
